## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sunakhajātaka* (Ja 242) is a short Pali birth story located in the Jātaka collection [Catalog; Fausböll 1879]. The canonical verse opens with the line *Bālo vatāyam sunakho ti* ("Foolish dog") [Fausböll 1879]. The framing commentary records that the Buddha delivered this teaching while residing at Jetavana about a dog that was sheltered and fed in the hall by the Ambala tower (*ambalakoṭṭhaka-āsanasālā*), where water-carriers had reared it from birth until it grew stout on donated food [Fausböll 1879].
